prompts.a:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: detailed full-color completion illustration for a Picross album, variant A of a Balut motif. Create exactly ONE standalone image, not a sheet.
Subject: Filipino balut, a cooked fertilized duck egg, presented in a large upright lower eggshell with the top and part of the front shell peeled away. Three-quarter view from slightly above. The shell is pale ivory with a subtly blue-green cast and a few fine natural speckles. The open interior clearly shows a generous golden ochre cooked yolk, a small compact curled grey-brown cooked duck embryo with a modest folded head and tiny closed beak, pale firm albumen and a little warm broth sheen. It must read as the prepared food, not a live bird hatching, not a cute fluffy yellow duckling. Gently descriptive culinary illustration; no blood, graphic tissue, horror or exaggerated anatomy. Keep the embryo integrated with the yolk and contained within the egg. Egg and opening are the dominant connected silhouette, centered, comfortably inside the canvas.
Style: warm quiet hand-drawn 2D gouache-and-ink illustration; confidently guided warm dark brown contours, clean strong coherent color areas, characterful proportions, refined interior linework, subtle natural shell texture and restrained warm shading. Detailed but calm, not photorealistic, not 3D, not pixel art, not a simplified icon. Main forms clearly separable and suitable for later abstraction without simplifying to a grid yet.
Background: genuine PNG transparency throughout outside the food; no white or cream rectangular background, no tabletop, plate, hands, props, garnish, cast-shadow patch, labels, text, watermark, frame or grid. Preserve opaque light shell and albumen. Clean antialiased alpha edges with no pale halo. Square framing with generous transparent outer margin.

Preserve light opaque shell and light albumen; do not erase them based on brightness. Keep delicate clean antialiased contour pixels, no brown halo or white fringe. No background, no glow, no shadow.
